title: Biochemistry and Pathophysiological Role of Specialized Pro-Resolving Lipid Mediators (SPMs) in Cardiovascular Disease
content: The essay reviews the biochemical and pathophysiological aspects of specialized pro-resolving lipid mediators (SPMs) – lipoxins, resolvins, protectins and maresins – in the context of cardiovascular diseases. It is shown that SPMs, which are formed from polyunsaturated fatty acids with the participation of lipoxygenases and cyclooxygenases, exert their action through specific G-protein-coupled receptors (ALX/FPR2, GPR32, ChemR23, GPR18), promoting efferocytosis, polarization of macrophages into the M2 phenotype and suppression of pro-inflammatory signaling pathways. Experimental data on the cardioprotective role of SPMs in atherosclerosis, myocardial infarction and heart failure are presented. At the same time, analytical and translational limitations are critically analyzed: ultralow concentrations of SPMs in biological fluids, methodological difficulties in quantitative determination, as well as contradictory data on the activation of their receptors. It is argued that further progress requires a transition from measuring concentrations to assessing functional activity and developing stable synthetic analogues and targeted delivery systems. The essay is intended for scientists in the fields of biochemistry, molecular biology, and cardiology.
